open_points.subject: NodeExecution trace cardinality after a cleanup-failure record is refused
open_points.text: “One NodeExecution per concluded element” contradicts “except a function execution during which the kernel stops because the store refused that record: it leaves none” and “Every concluded attempt at an element ... writes exactly one NodeExecution M23.”
open_points.question: Does the cleanup-failed execution whose record was refused count as a concluded attempt that must later receive a NodeExecution, or is it permanently absent from the trace?
options: The failed execution leaves no NodeExecution; recovery reuses the same attempt ordinal and only the re-execution is recorded.
Recovery first records the missing cleanup failure, then re-executes as a later attempt.
The record refusal means the execution is not considered concluded, so the one-record-per-conclusion statements must explicitly exclude it.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the new exception as authoritative: leave no record, regard the attempt as unconcluded for trace purposes, and reuse its ordinal on recovery.

witness.initial: A running run reaches a function element; sandbox cleanup is unconfirmed, and the store refuses the cleanup_failed NodeExecution.
events: module:sandbox returns crashed with cleanup_failed and stop_required.
module:runs attempts to store the NodeExecution; module:store refuses it.
The host starts the kernel again, and module:runs recovers the run.
outcomes: The trace permanently omits the first execution; recovery executes the function again under the same next attempt number.
The first execution must still acquire a NodeExecution because every concluded attempt has exactly one; any re-execution is a later attempt.
witness.observer: The owner or agent reading the trace and attempt numbers

open_points.subject: Recovery of a run function after its cleanup-failure record was refused
open_points.text: “recovery executes the element again” contradicts “The next start finds that element concluded and does not execute it again” and “a cleanup failure stops the kernel at most once per element and never loops.”
open_points.question: After the cleanup_failed record is refused, must startup recovery re-execute the element, and may repeated cleanup or store failures stop successive starts more than once?
options: Re-execute whenever no concluded record exists; successive starts may stop repeatedly until a record is stored.
Treat the cleanup failure as concluded despite the missing record; do not re-execute it.
Create a separate durable recovery marker whose successful storage prevents re-execution.
open_points.default_guess: Re-execute whenever the record is absent; remove the claims that the next start always finds a conclusion and that cleanup failure can stop the kernel at most once.

witness.initial: A function element has no concluded record because storage of its cleanup_failed NodeExecution was refused.
events: The first execution reports unconfirmed cleanup.
The store refuses its NodeExecution, and the kernel stops.
Startup recovery executes the element again.
The second execution also has unconfirmed cleanup, but this time its record can be stored.
outcomes: The second execution occurs and stops the kernel again before a later start advances dependants.
The next start treats the element as already concluded, does not execute it again, and advances its dependants as upstream_failed.
witness.observer: The host operator sees the additional stopped start; run readers see whether a second execution occurred

open_points.subject: Scope of automatic re-execution for trials and admission executions
open_points.text: “If that record cannot be stored, the element has no concluded record and recovery executes it again, as it does every function element without a concluded record” appears beside “the module that called sandbox.execute_function writes the execution's record ... functions the TrialExecution,” but startup offers only capability:effects.recover_in_flight_attempts and capability:runs.recover_running_runs.
open_points.question: Does the new recovery promise cover TrialExecutions from an explicit try or admission, and if so which module operation durably identifies and re-executes those interrupted executions at startup?
options: It covers only function elements of runs; an explicit try is not recovered, and admission runs again only on a later submission.
It also covers admission executions; module:functions needs a startup recovery capability and durable admission-progress state.
It covers both admission and explicit tries; module:functions needs durable request/execution state and startup recovery for both.
open_points.default_guess: Limit automatic startup re-execution to function elements of runs; keep admission retry on the next submission and leave an interrupted explicit try as an internal-error response with no automatic retry.

witness.initial: An agent explicitly tries an implementation on one case; cleanup is unconfirmed and the store refuses the TrialExecution.
events: The sandbox returns cleanup_failed with stop_required.
module:store refuses the TrialExecution, and module:surface answers internal_error and stops.
The host restarts the kernel without another agent request.
outcomes: The function is executed again during startup recovery and a TrialExecution is eventually recorded.
Startup recovery touches only EffectAttempts and runs; the try is never repeated unless an agent issues another try.
witness.observer: The trying agent and later readers of the trial evidence
